Billy Civil Parish

Guide to **Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland ancestry, family history, and genealogy**. Parish registers, transcripts, baptism records, marriage records, and burial records.

## History

Billy is a parish, partly in the barony of Carey, but chiefly in that of Lower Dunluce, poor union of Coleraine, county of Antrim and province of Ulster; containing the post town of Bushmills and a portion of Dunserverick.

This parish was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union, that comprised also the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, together forming the corps of the archdeaconry of Connor. The rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now constitute the corps of the archdeaconry. In the Roman Catholic divisions the parish forms part of the district of Coleraine. There are meeting houses for Presbyterians, for Covenanters, and Wesleyan Methodists.
